note: DRY-COVERAGE-PLAN.md item 12.C.4: the profiles `chaos.py` runs a driver through, each with what the contract expects of it. `applies` says which transports a profile is a fault of: real TCP retransmits, so it never delivers a lost, duplicated, reordered, truncated or corrupt byte, and those are the datagram transports' (UDP, SocketCAN, raw Ethernet) and a serial line's. A CAN frame carries its own CRC, so a corrupt one never reaches a controller and `corrupt` is not listed for it. `expect.outage` means the link stops carrying data and the driver must say so; `expect.stop` means the stop path is tried with the link like this; `min_ok_fraction` is for a poor link that is not a dead one. Every profile with a subject that moves also has the age check: an OK read may not be older than the driver's own staleness bound. Delay and jitter are listed twice, at the magnitude of a network (50 ms, 30 ms ± 25) and at the magnitude of a bus or a serial line (2 ms, 1 ms ± 1 — a USB-CAN adapter's own latency, inside a driver's few-millisecond answer window): a bus a gateway has made tens of milliseconds long is not the bus such a driver was written for, and `sync_window_ms` is how an integrator says so.
